arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Thompson argued North Carolina law designates state officers as necessary parties.
Ms. Boyce argued the Attorney General adequately represents the state's interest.
Justice Sotomayor questioned the adequacy of the Attorney General's representation.
Chief Justice Roberts asked about political disagreements between state representatives.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: North Carolina law names state officers as necessary parties in legal challenges to state statutes. the sides that brought the case argue this law grants them a right to intervene in federal court. the opposing sides argue the Attorney General adequately represents the state's interest. The Court must decide if state law creates a federal right to intervene.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of state legislative power in federal courts. It determines whether state statutes can create federal procedural rights. The outcome shapes how states defend their laws against constitutional challenges.
